notProven.description: The header's `this check fails iff DISPATCH_BODY_MAX > maxInputChars` is falsified by two compiling trees, found by thermonuclear-deep-review and reproduced by the reviewer. Tree A, dispatch-tools.ts: a `/* ... */` block holding a stale `export const DISPATCH_BODY_MAX = 10;` above a live `export const DISPATCH_BODY_MAX = 99_000;` - the check reads the commented copy and prints `body limit 10 (...:2) fits the embedder's 19000`, exit 0, while the live cap is 99000. Tree B, embed.go: a `/* ... */` block holding `maxInputChars = 99000` above a live `maxInputChars int = 8000` - exit 0 reporting the embedder at 99000 while it cuts at 8000. Both need two simultaneous faults, and each fault alone is fatal: a live declaration the patterns cannot read is refused (`declares no <const> this check can read`), and a readable stale copy beside a readable live one is refused (`declares <const> more than once`). A `//`-commented copy never matches at all. This is the same comment-versus-string blindness the architect withdrew the comment assertion over, in the declaration read, and no fix exists inside the agreed design without parsing the language. Recorded rather than fixed; the header sentence is the fast-follow.

The check reads DISPATCH_BODY_MAX from the TypeScript source alone. The cap the server enforces is the generated copy contracts.DispatchBodyMax, held by `bun run check:go` in the `contracts` job, which main's ruleset does not require. Named in the script's header; outside this issue.
